assumptions: Orders, their delivery station and delivery day come from the middle mile, for each staffing plan (real 2023 orders, assumed network).

Each customer is a business at one fixed census tract center inside its station's delivery area: everywhere a van can reach in 45 minutes (OpenRouteService isochrone; a radius if that file is missing). Tracts are picked with odds matching their population (ACS 2022 5-year), so customers follow where people live. Which tract each customer gets is random but the same in every run.
A stop is every parcel for one customer on one day. A stop larger than one van is split across vans.

Vans carry 250 pairs of shoes and work a 10 hour shift. A stop takes 12 minutes plus 0.2 minutes per pair. Road distances and drive times come from OpenRouteService (fetch_road_matrix.py); they leave out traffic, so van times are optimistic. Without that file, distance is 1.3 times straight line at 35 km/h.

An owned van costs $380 a day whether or not it is used. A contracted van costs $600 on the days it is called. Each km costs fuel at that week's real 2023 US diesel price (FRED) at about 18 miles a gallon, plus an assumed $0.25 for tires, maintenance and wear. The day rates are hypothetical.
A parcel carrier (like UPS Ground) is the alternative to running vans: $9 per order plus $0.90 per pair, assumed.
